Hawker Hurricane: United Kingdom. The Air Ministry ordered Hawker's Interceptor Monoplane in late 1934, and the prototype Hurricane K5083 performed its maiden flight on 6 November 1935.
Who is credited with discovering Norma?

Norma (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is Latin for normal, referring to a right angle, and is variously considered to represent a rule, a carpenter's square, a set square or a level.
Who is credited with discovering Aspartame?
Aspartame: James M. Schlatter. Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Who is credited with discovering Histamine?
Histamine: Henry Hallett Dale. Histamine or histamin is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.
About 5 million tonnes of acetic acid are produced annually largely to make this compound, most commonly in polymer form — what is it?
Acetate is a salt formed by the combination of acetic acid with a base (e.g. sodium hydroxide), an ester of acetic acid, or the anion CH3COO- found in solution.

Native to South America but cultivated in Europe since the 17th century for its fragrant oil, this flowering member of the verbena family is better known by a common name referencing a citrus fruit — what's its scientific name?
Aloysia citrodora is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
This scientific discipline bridges biology and sociology, studying human behavior, cultures, societies, and languages across time. What field is it?

Anthropology is the scientific study of humanity that crosses biology and sociology, concerned with human behavior, human biology, cultures, societies, and linguistics, in both the present and past, including archaic humans.

It's one of the oldest natural sciences, recruiting math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything that originates beyond Earth's atmosphere — from comets and quasars to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Astronomy is a natural science that studies celestial objects and the phenomena that occur in the cosmos.
This perennial flowering plant species, native to Eurasia and growing up to four feet tall, includes cultivated varieties used for sugar, its edible root, and its edible leaves — what species is it?
Beta vulgaris (beet) is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Betoideae of the family Amaranthaceae.
Members of this decapod infraorder tuck a tiny tail-like abdomen under a hard thorax and end their front legs in pincers — which true creatures are they?
Brachyura is an infraorder of decapod crustaceans comprising the true crabs.
This opportunistic yeast lives harmlessly in the gut and mouth of most healthy adults, but can turn pathogenic in immunocompromised people, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
Famous for color-shifting camouflage and zygodactylous, pincer-like feet, which family of roughly 200 Old World lizard species is this?
Chameleon (family Chamaeleonidae) are a distinctive and highly specialized clade of Old World lizards with 200 species described as of June 2015.

Largely self-taught and grinding his own lenses from spare parts on a Kansas farm, this astronomer's homemade skills landed him at Lowell Observatory — where his 1930 survey turned up the first known body in the Kuiper belt; who was he?

Clyde Tombaugh (February 4, 1906 - January 17, 1997) was an American astronomer and telescope maker, best known for discovering Pluto in 1930, marking the first detection of what would eventually be recognized as the Kuiper belt.
Derived from Greek words meaning universe and study of, this scientific and philosophical field examines the nature of existence at the grandest scale — what is it called?
Cosmology (from Ancient Greek (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and - (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
This Asian canid stands apart from true dogs: a convex rather than concave skull, no third lower molar, and single-cusped upper molars — once it roamed into Europe. What is it?
Dhole (dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.
Which natural science examines how living things relate to their environment, spanning the individual, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere levels?
Ecology (from Ancient Greek (okos) 'house' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the natural science of the relationships among living organisms and their environment.

This Austrian physicist devised a foundational equation for calculating a quantum system's wave function and coined the term 'quantum entanglement,' sharing the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac — who is he?
Erwin Schrödinger (12 August 1887 - 4 January 1961), sometimes written as Schroedinger or Schrodinger, was an Austrian theoretical physicist who developed fundamental results in quantum theory.

This Arabic term describes the human interpretation and practice of Islamic religious law, expanded through jurists' scholarly reasoning and expressed in the rulings they issue on questions of faith. What is this field called?
Fiqh is the term for Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
Practitioners of this discipline monitor crustal motion, tides, and polar shifts to maintain accurate global positioning reference frames — what is this field called?
Geodesy (jee-) or geodetics is the science of measuring and representing the geometry, gravity, and spatial orientation of the Earth in temporally varying 3D space.
Endemic to Africa and among the oldest of the gallinaceous birds, this family branched off before New World quail evolutionarily — name the birds?
Guinea fowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
Planted for land reclamation thanks to its nitrogen-fixing, erosion-resisting root system, this deciduous shrub genus's berries also show up in human and animal food products — what genus is it?
Hippophae is a genus of flowering plants in the family Elaeagnaceae.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women as a physical illness in the 19th century, this term for ungovernable emotional excess later became the focus of research by Freud and Charcot — what is this condition called?
Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

This American economist gave his name to a model for censored dependent variables — the 'tobit' — and advised the Council of Economic Advisers while championing government action to head off recessions. Who was he?

James Tobin (March 5, 1918 - March 11, 2002) was an American economist who served on the Council of Economic Advisers and consulted with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and taught at Yale University.
A founder of modern geometric analysis, this American mathematician won the 2019 Abel Prize for pioneering work in geometric PDEs and gauge theory — who is she?
Karen Uhlenbeck (born August 24, 1942) is an American mathematician and one of the founders of modern geometric analysis.

A Cornell-trained engineer and Atlanta factory superintendent, this man was wrongly convicted of a young employee's murder, then kidnapped from prison and lynched in a case now central to American antisemitism — who was he?

Leo Frank (April 17, 1884 - August 17, 1915) was an American lynching victim wrongly convicted of the murder of 13-year-old Mary Phagan, an employee in a factory in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was the superintendent.
Born in Winnipeg and trained at King's College London, this physicist and chemist joined the Manhattan Project in 1942 to conduct experiments with uranium — who is he?
Louis Slotin (1 December 1910 - 30 May 1946) was a Canadian physicist and chemist who took part in the Manhattan Project.
He helped uncover the Antarctic ozone hole and shared a 1995 Nobel for exposing the danger CFCs pose to the ozone layer — which Mexican chemist?
Mario Molina (19 March 1943 - 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
Connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum to the pons, this brainstem structure plays a role in vision, hearing, and staying alert -- what is it called?
Midbrain is the uppermost portion of the brainstem connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum with the pons.

Chemically known as bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, this organosulfur compound is a potent alkylating agent and carcinogen with no preventive antidote — protection relies entirely on covering the skin and airways. Name this notorious chemical warfare agent?
Mustard gas are names commonly used for the organosulfur chemical compound bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, which has the chemical structure S(CH2CH2Cl)2, as well as other species.
Element 102 honors the inventor of dynamite, and its short-lived isotope 255 — with a 3-minute half-life — is the one chemists actually prefer to work with. Which synthetic actinide is it?
Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Dubbed the father of nuclear chemistry, he studied under Ernest Rutherford before helping identify the radioactive elements radium, thorium, and protactinium — who is he?
Otto Hahn (8 March 1879 - 28 July 1968) was a German chemist who was a pioneer in the field of radiochemistry.
Listed in the Dictionary of Fungi as containing over 300 species, this mold genus produces a compound that stops bacterial growth and also flavors certain cheeses — which genus?
Penicillium is a genus of ascomycetous fungi that is part of the mycobiome of many species and is of major importance in the natural environment, in food spoilage, and in food and drug production.
Equal to one-eighth of a gallon in both the imperial and US customary systems, this unit of volume is just over 20% larger in Britain than it is in America — name it?
Pint (symbol pt, sometimes abbreviated as p) is a unit of volume or capacity in both the imperial and United States customary measurement systems.
Originating on Gran Canaria and Tenerife, this large Spanish mastiff-type breed was traditionally used to guard property, herd livestock, and, legally until 1936, fight other dogs — what breed is it?
Presa Canario is a Spanish breed of large dog of mastiff or catch dog type.
It can form not just from rain but from mist, spray, or dew, and though we usually see an arc, it can actually be a full circle — what optical phenomenon is it?
Rainbow is an optical phenomenon caused by refraction, internal reflection and dispersion of light in water droplets resulting in a continuous spectrum of light appearing in the sky.
Named for its type genus, this plant family of nearly 4,800 species includes the trees and shrubs behind apples, pears, plums, cherries, and peaches — what family is it?
Rosaceae is a family of flowering plants that includes 4,828 known species in 91 genera.
This synthetic element, atomic number 106, is so fleeting that only a few atoms exist at a time and decay within minutes — and it's named for an American nuclear chemist; what is it?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Doctors recommend covering your elbow rather than your hands to block this involuntary, explosive rush of air from spreading illness through the air. What is this reflex called?
Sneeze (also known as sternutation) is a semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth, usually caused by foreign particles irritating the nasal mucosa.
This muscular, hollow organ in the upper digestive tract handles the gastric phase of digestion, and gives us the medical prefix 'gastric' from its Ancient Greek name — name the organ?
Stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.
Sporting beaded antennae and a pale, soft-bodied worker caste, these decaying-wood eaters belong to the order Isoptera and are really highly derived cockroaches — what are they?
Termite are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or contact with infected cat feces, this disease can be especially dangerous to a developing baby if a woman is infected during pregnancy — what is it?
Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii, an apicomplexan.
This type of blood vessel usually carries deoxygenated blood toward the heart — except in the pulmonary and fetal circulation, where it carries oxygen-rich blood instead — what is it?
Vein is a blood vessel in the circulatory system of humans and most other animals that carries blood towards the heart.
This noble gas, found in trace amounts in Earth's atmosphere, powers arc lamps, serves as a rare anesthetic, and was the first of its family coaxed into a genuine chemical compound — which element?
Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Named for the skull-shaped marking on its thorax and first classified by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, this large moth was immortalized on the poster for 'The Silence of the Lambs' — which insect?
Acherontia atropos: Species of moth. It is most commonly identified by the vaguely skull-shaped pattern adorning the thorax, the characteristic from which its common and scientific names are derived.
Scientifically named Gadus chalcogrammus, this schooling member of the cod family gathers in massive numbers in the eastern Bering Sea — which fish?
Alaska pollock: Species of fish. The Alaska pollock also known as Pacific pollock or walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) is a marine fish species of the cod genus Gadus and family Gadidae.
Native to the Americas, this plant is better known by its common names common ragweed, annual ragweed, or low ragweed — what is its scientific name?
Ambrosia artemisiifolia: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family.

Named from Greek words meaning "unlike other shrimp," this extinct arthropod from the Burgess Shale had swimming flaps, big compound eyes and grasping frontal appendages, reaching over a foot long — which prehistoric predator?
Anomalocaris: Extinct genus of cambrian radiodont.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this small tree bears bell-shaped rose-to-purple flowers and a ridged fruit that forms star-shaped slices when cut crosswise — which species?
Averrhoa carambola: Species of tree. It is a small tree or shrub that grows 5 to 12 m (16 to 39 ft) tall, with rose to red-purple flowers.

When no one else had the staff for it, this American lawyer volunteered to prosecute the Einsatzgruppen trial at Nuremberg, then spent decades championing an International Criminal Court — who was he?

In this distributed ledger, each record holds a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering a single block would require rewriting every block that follows — making the data nearly tamper-proof. What is it?
Blockchain: Distributed data store for digital transactions.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?

Ranging from the hefty black species of the Amazon basin to the diminutive dwarf species just over a metre long, these Central and South American relatives of alligators make up their own reptile subfamily — what are they called?
Caiman: Subfamily of reptiles. The black caiman is the largest caiman species in the world and is found in the slow-moving rivers and lakes that surround the Amazon basin.

Born in London, raised in Milan, and self-taught in web design, this Catholic teenager built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles before dying of leukemia at fifteen — he was beatified in 2020. Who was he?
Which second-generation antihistamine for hay fever kicks in within half an hour but is more likely than fexofenadine or loratadine to cause drowsiness?

Cetirizine: Antihistamine medication. Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
With about 3,400 species in over 520 genera, this insect family includes nearly every member of its group except two species in a small sister taxon — which family?
Used to treat gout, familial Mediterranean fever, and pericarditis, this medication has such a narrow therapeutic index that its injectable form was pulled from the US market in 2008. What is it?
Colchicine: Medication mainly used to treat gout. The American College of Rheumatology recommends colchicine, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or steroids in the treatment of gout.
Home to crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, this bird family boasts a brain-to-body ratio rivaling great apes, and one of its members even passed the mirror self-recognition test — what family is this?

A Scottish biologist, classicist and mathematician who pioneered theoretical biology, he's remembered for his 1917 book On Growth and Form, which opened the way to explaining how patterns and body structures take shape — who was he?
D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson: Scottish biologist, mathematician, and classics scholar.

This group of microalgae generates roughly a fifth to a half of Earth's oxygen each year, and its dead shells drift on Saharan winds to fertilize the entire Amazon basin with millions of tons of dust annually. What are they?
Diatom: Single-celled alga with a silica cell wall.
The only living relative of the extinct Steller's sea cow, this seagrass-grazing marine mammal is most abundant in the waters of northern Australia — what is it?
Dugong: Species of marine mammal. It is one of four living species of the order Sirenia, which also includes three species of manatees.
Co-founding Mattel with his wife Ruth, this inventor helped bring Barbie, Hot Wheels, and Chatty Cathy to toy shelves — who is he?
Elliot Handler: American inventor and business magnate (1916–2011)
Made by yeast fermenting sugars and once used as a general anesthetic, this colorless flammable liquid is the world's second most consumed drug, behind only caffeine — what is it?
Proposed in 1724 by a physicist who set water's freezing point at 32 degrees and boiling at 212, this temperature scale was originally anchored to a freezing brine solution — which scale?
Fahrenheit: Temperature scale. The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale based on one proposed in 1724 by the physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit (1686–1736).
Grown for both food and fiber, this plant's seeds are pressed into linseed oil while its stem fibers are woven into linen for sheets and clothing. What plant is it?
This Canadian physician and author has written five books linking childhood trauma to conditions like ADHD and addiction, though critics question the evidence behind some claims — who is he?
Caused by a genetic variant in the UGT1A1 gene, this harmless liver condition slows the breakdown of bilirubin and can trigger jaundice during stress, exercise, or fasting — what is it called?
Gilbert's syndrome: Medical condition. It is typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and occasionally in an autosomal dominant pattern depending on the type of variant.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.

Made by fusing heavy nuclei in tiny quantities, this superheavy element 108 has a special isotope whose "magic numbers" of protons and neutrons make its deformed nucleus unusually stable — what is it?
Hassium: Chemical element with atomic number 108 (Hs)
Its name means 'river horse' in Ancient Greek, yet this semiaquatic sub-Saharan giant — the largest even-toed ungulate alive — is more closely tied to pigs than to horses; what is it?
Hippopotamus: Species of large semi-aquatic mammal.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.

This Dutch microscopist showed that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one animal, pioneered the microscope in dissections, and in 1658 became the first to observe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam: Dutch biologist and microscopist (1637–1680)
Committed to accuracy and verification, this occupation and set of methods involves gathering and distributing the day's news — what field is it?
Journalism: Production of reports on current events.
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
An oily alkaloid from nightshade plants like tobacco, it doubles as a potent insect neurotoxin and once served as an insecticide, inspiring the neonicotinoid pesticides — what is it?
Nicotine: Chemical stimulant produced by some plants.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.

Detected by receptors in your muscles, tendons, and joints, this sense tells your brain where your body is in space, working alongside vision and balance to keep you upright and coordinated — what's it called?
Proprioception: Sense of self-movement, force, and body position.
Found in notable amounts in capers, red onions, and kale, this bitter-tasting plant flavonol is a popular ingredient in dietary supplements — what compound?
Quercetin: Chemical compound. It is found in many fruits, vegetables, leaves, seeds, and grains; capers, red onions, and kale are common foods containing appreciable amounts of it.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Caused by the same Group A strep behind strep throat, this childhood illness brings a sandpapery red rash and a bumpy tongue — what is it?
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.
For 30 years this English theoretical astrophysicist held Cambridge's most prestigious academic post—the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. Who?
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
A British-American structural biologist who shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for revealing the structure of the ribosome, he later served as President of the Royal Society — who is he?
Once nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse,' this British sighthound is believed to have the fastest idle-to-running acceleration of any dog breed — which breed?
Whippet: British breed of dog. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this strategist was sought out three times by Liu Bei and helped engineer victory at the Battle of Red Cliffs — who is he?
Zhuge Liang: Chinese statesman and strategist (181–234)
